comparison.appsup-dart/openid_client: Dart IO/browser design plus published platform support across mobile/desktop/web

comparison.Bdaya-Dev/oidc: OidcUserManager, login/logout, user changes, refresh-token rotation
comparison.appsup-dart/openid_client: Client/Credential/Flow primitives, token refresh and RP-initiated logout
comparison.verdict: Bdaya maps more directly to a full session boundary

comparison.appsup-dart/openid_client: proof does not treat persistence as a complete session-store abstraction
comparison.verdict: Bdaya lower semantic adapter work; Library must still keep storage ownership explicit

comparison.Bdaya-Dev/oidc: federated platform packages plus OIDC/runtime helpers
unit/E2E tests, GitHub Actions and Dependabot at pinned tree
comparison.appsup-dart/openid_client: tests plus Travis config; current CI health not verified

comparison.Bdaya-Dev/oidc: fuller semantics but higher SDK floor
comparison.appsup-dart/openid_client: lower SDK coupling but more auth.session adapter policy required
comparison.verdict: trade-off depends on host compatibility and desired boundary thickness

human_recommendation.reason: Its UserManager, refresh, logout, configurable store and all-platform federated implementation map most directly to a full auth.session boundary.
human_recommendation.alternative_reason: Prefer when lower framework coupling and a thinner provider-neutral OIDC primitive are more important than built-in session-management semantics.

limitations: auth.session.v1 is currently only a draft logical Library contract; no unstated API semantics were invented
Upstream CI workflow/config presence is evidence, not a claim that every upstream job is currently green
outcome: Both candidates shortlisted. No absolute winner: Bdaya-Dev/oidc is the preferred full-session candidate; openid_client is the thinner lower-coupling alternative.
